preconditions.description: The input must be a string, integer, or float. If it is a number, it is converted to its string representation.

postconditions.expression: all(c.islower() or c.isdigit() for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every character in the output string is either a lowercase letter or a digit.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] == '_' for i in range(1, len(return_value)) if return_value[i-1].isupper() and return_value[i].islower())
postconditions.description: Every underscore in the output string appears between a lowercase letter and an uppercase letter in the original CamelCase string (or between a digit and a letter).

postconditions.expression: return_value == str(input) if not isinstance(input, str) else True
postconditions.description: If the input is not a string (e.g., a number), the output is the string representation of the input.

postconditions.expression: return_value == ''.join([c.lower() if c.isupper() else c for c in input]) if len(input) == 1 else True
postconditions.description: If the input is a single uppercase letter, the output is the lowercase version of that letter.

postconditions.expression: return_value == ''.join([c.lower() if c.isupper() else c for c in input]).replace(' ', '_') if ' ' in input else True
postconditions.description: If the input contains spaces, they are replaced with underscores in the output.

postconditions.expression: return_value == ''.join([c.lower() if c.isupper() else c for c in input]).replace(' ', '_') if ' ' in input else True
postconditions.description: The output string is derived by inserting underscores before every uppercase letter (except the first) in the input CamelCase string, and converting all letters to lowercase.

postconditions.expression: return_value == input if input.islower() and '_' not in input else True
postconditions.description: If the input is already in snake_case (all lowercase with underscores), the output is identical to the input.
